Полиглузама Гидрохлорид Pharmacopoeias. In Eur. (see p.vii). Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Chitosan Hydrochloride). The chloride salt of an unbranched binary heteropolysaccharide consisting of the two units N-acetyl-D-glucosamine and D-glucosamine, obtained by partial deacetylation of chitin, normally leading to a degree of deacetylation of 70.0 to 95.0%. Chitin is extracted from the shells of shrimp and crab. A white or almost white fine powder. Sparingly soluble in water; practically insoluble in alcohol. A 1% solution in water has a pH of 4.0 to 6.0. Store in airtight contain- ers at a temperature of 2° to 8°. Protect from light. Profile Poliglusam is a polysaccharide composed of polymers of glu- cosamine and N-acetylglucosamine produced by partial deacetylation of chitin. It is manufactured commercially by chemical treatment of crustacean shells. Poliglusam is under in- vestigation as a pharmaceutical excipient for formulations in- cluding oral dosage forms and gene carrier systems. It has been used as a dietary supplement in preparations for obesity and hy- percholesterolaemia. ◊ References. 1. Ylitalo R, et al. Cholesterol-lowering properties and safety of chitosan. Arzneimittelforschung 2002; 52: 1–7. 2. Jull AB, et al. Chitosan for overweight or obesity. Available in The Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews; Issue 3.
